trust_decision.summary: The Rsdoctor report server decides whether a caller may read the project's build metadata and module source, and at the pinned commit it decides nothing: the connect app answers every API route with 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' plus 'Allow-Credentials: true', and the socket.io channel accepts any client with 'cors: { origin: "*" }'.

landing_point.why: The single line 'this.app.use(cors());' is the only access decision in the report server; an engineer reading 'unauthenticated HTTP API that exposes project source' looks here first and replaces it with an origin allow-list.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: createServer/getPortSync in @rsdoctor/utils are generic local-tool build helpers used by other packages; the access check belongs in the report server's own app, so a solver can leave the loopback bind and the EADDRINUSE rejection unfixed there.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The report UI fetches every page over the socket.io channel (getSocket(socketPort).emit(api, ...)) and the MCP server connects to 'ws://localhost:<port>' using only the port from .rsdoctor/mcp.json; any token or Origin/Host requirement added at the WS handshake breaks both unless the URL is plumbed through the manifest (the main-branch commit had to add __SOCKET__URL__), and restricting hosts to 'localhost' only would also break the LAN-IP access that the reference allow-list deliberately keeps (192.168.1.10:3000 is accepted).

O6_input_shapes: Host / ':authority' header: absent, 'localhost:3000', 'foo.localhost:3000', '127.0.0.1:3000', '[::1]:3000', '192.168.1.10:3000', 'evil.example.com:3000', and non-string (array) values
Origin header: undefined (allowed), 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>', 'http://foo.localhost:<port>' (must match Host), 'https://example.com', and array values
WebSocket/socket URL: token query present, absent, or wrong
server.cors config: undefined (default local allow-list), false, true, partial object (e.g. only credentials), object with a custom origin

O8_uncovered_routes.route: socket.io channel: every ServerAPI event is registered and answered over the WS transport (SocketAPILoader.loadAPIData) with 'cors: { origin: "*" }' and no Host/Origin/token verification - the same source-code sink (/api/graph/module/code etc.) reached without the HTTP app's middleware
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the HTTP API; the socket is the report UI's own transport, so a solver can argue it is a separate, UI-only channel that the published v1.x fix never touched (602eb30 only edits the HTTP app and @rsdoctor/utils).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, sibling directory: packages/sdk/src/sdk/server/socket/ vs packages/sdk/src/sdk/server/

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second raw connect route mounted like /__open-in-editor, registered before or outside the guarded middleware
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already mounts a hand-written app.use route next to the router, and the fix had to reorder router.setup() ahead of the static handler; a maintainer adding another helper route would repeat that pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: proxy()/get()/post() registering a route that writes its own ACAO header
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: wrapNextHandleFunction sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' by hand today; a new server-push or proxy route would copy that wrapper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A server subclass that overrides bootstrap() and rebuilds the middleware chain
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RsdoctorSlaveServer already subclasses RsdoctorServer and overrides openClientPage; overriding bootstrap is the obvious next move when slave servers need different ports.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second createApp()/createServer() factory used for a standalone or diff report
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: createApp is exported and separate from createServer, inviting another construction path that would not inherit the SDK's middleware.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The webpack plugin's own RsdoctorSDK construction site (twin of the rspack plugin, which the fix did update)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It duplicates the rspack-plugins' option wiring almost line for line; any new server option has to be threaded here too, exactly as the fix threaded it through packages/rspack-plugin/src/plugin.ts.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new 'push data to clients' API that emits to the socket without going through the guarded HTTP route handler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SendAPIDataToClient already broadcasts arbitrary data to every socket client; the same shape is an easy template for another route.

O9_family: Information exposure through missing access control on a developer tool's local HTTP/WebSocket API (CWE-200 / CWE-668): cross-origin and DNS-rebinding read of build metadata and module source
